So... Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium is another collection of 30+ Capcom Arcade Classics. And like the first Stadium, I really enjoy it for what it is. I had a problem with the first Stadium where my game would randomly freeze for a few seconds every so often while I was connected to the internet, and 2nd Stadium doesn't do that to me. So I'm gonna go into pros and cons, but before I do I'm gonna address a big elephant in the room...

[h1]Stadium or Fighting Collection?[/h1]
Many have taken notice that Stadium 2 has 6 of the same games as the Fighting Collection, such as 3 Darkstalkers titles, Super Gem Fighter, and such and it only released a month after Fighting Collection. If you just wanna play these games, you should get the Fighting Collection as it has a bunch more settings you can play around with such as improved controls, online play, and easy-to-select secret characters. Stadium only has Rewind, Speed Change, and Invincibility. I don't recommend you go out of your way to get those overlapping games on their own unless you just wanna have a complete Stadium set or mess around with Invincibility. If you already didn't have a copy, then maybe, but for these games, Fighting Collection is superior.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
-32 classic arcade games that are mostly fun
-Customizable settings, same as the first Stadium
-Improved Time, Score, and Special Challenge Modes (This got ported into the first Stadium too)
-Invcincibility Setting DLC for all 32 games, and it was free when I got it this time!
-Rewind, Speed Change, and Infinite Coins if you want them

[h1]The Meh[/h1]
-No online multiplayer, Remote Play Together is your best bet.

[h1]Cons[/h1]
-Came out 1 month after the Fighting Collection with half of that collection's library
-Any altered assets from 1st Stadium and Fighting Collection still altered here
-Overlapping games from Fighting Collection have more options than their Stadium counterparts

8/10

Capcom Arcade Stadium, both 1 and 2, are solid collections of games that I am not disappointed in owning. I love to play arcade games, but have a difficult time mastering them. With these collections, I can play a wide variety of games - bullet hells, fighting games, platformers, Puyo Puyo-likes, Tetris-likes, Match 3s - and master my timing and skills in these games which I still fare horribly at.

Having a rewind/slow-mo/fast-forward feature is very much appreciated, one that I also loved in SEGA Genesis and Mega Drive Classics (which I still own). I'm not very good at Street Fighter, for instance, but I can better practice the Special Moves in slow motion (I have no idea how to execute them properly yet, and I've been playing SF for about three years now). I can also rewind, if a move I make is not well executed.

Some games I don't really like, such as Darkstalkers (although I appreciated Felicia's innocent, playful personality), but I'll almost always play a Mega Man game, and I know that there are two in these collections!

[i]PLEASE NOTE: One con about this title is that it uses The Enigma Protector, a type of DRM Capcom is using on older titles in place of Denuvo Anti-Tamper. However, I would not be too worried about it, as it is not super aggressive and can be defeated with anti-DRM tools if necessary - let me stress for legal reasons that I am NOT recommending this and do not endorse piracy or cheating, but if you're only playing offline AND not sharing the software, then it can be done - but even with Enigma in the game, all it really is meant to do is prevent cheating in the ranks, so I say leave it be.[/i]

The Capcom Arcade Stadiums tend to get a rather eh rep, and some of it was deserved up to a point in time, but honestly, I think now these are great ways of playing Capcom's arcade greats. They're especially fun when trying the challenges!

Do they devalue Capcom's other collections? Honestly, no. I think the point is for these to have a different focus from stuff like Capcom Fighting Collection's online VS play - you can still do that locally for funsies, but you get the most out of practicing your favorite games and recording your all-time best runs for the world to see - and for other players to challenge! Sure, the bot plague extended to these compilations a bit, but let's be real: I would NEVER count those lazy clowns in anything competitive. If you can beat real people's challenges, that's worth some pride.

Parting words: I hope that someday we can get more compilations of games that include spinoffs of fan-favorite game series. Seeing the MegaMan arcade games rereleased for the first time since, what, *freaking MegaMan Anniversary Collection of all things* is seriously awesome.

So anyone that didn't check the game's official website will feel robbed and lied to, and rightfully so. 

In regards to the Stadium itself, I feel it to be a redundancy, specially since pretty much the entirety of it's content, new menu music, backgrounds, emojis, and in-game unlockables like the borders and screen options could have all very well have been added to the first one, this makes it feel like the experience was cut in half, and for some bizarre reason with games priced 2€ more expensive too.

So, I like Capcom Arcade Stadium 2. I liked the 1st one as well. I don't need more than 15 minutes to know that much. It does more of what I liked about the 1st iteration. That said, I'm worried about the overall reviews that'll be incoming for this one for two reasons. 1st off, the free hub download followed by optional transactions for games removed the main barrier of entry keeping pretty much every game from getting review bombed. It's not something people pay to do. 2nd, and more importantly, a very significant portion of this game's releases are also in prior collections. Most notoriously, the overlap between this collection and the Fighting Collection (the Dark Stalkers collection) defies reason, considering they're only a few weeks apart in release. I like this title, and I've purchased and liked all of Capcom's retro bundles, from Mega Man to Beatemups to here. If Capcom keeps making preventable mistakes that keep their releases from performing well, we might not see more, and that's probably the worst thing about the Arcade Stadiums - that Capcom will draw the wrong conclusion from all the red thumbs.
